title: Testing designs with test doubles
idea: A unit test checks one class in isolation by injecting test doubles for its collaborators; TDD writes that failing test first, then the code, then tidies.

analogy.text: A car seat is tested on a rig with a crash dummy, not a real driver. The dummy records every force it feels.
analogy.breaks: A dummy only behaves as you scripted it, never like the real thing.

points: Inject collaborators through the constructor so a test can pass in doubles.
A fake is a small working version; a stub returns canned answers.
A spy or mock records calls, so the test checks what was sent.
TDD loops red, green, refactor: failing test, smallest fix, then clean up.

messages.label: new SignupService(fake, spy)
messages.note: Arrange: the test builds the class and hands it doubles instead of a database and an SMTP client.

messages.label: register('ada@x.io')
messages.note: Act: call the one public method under test.

messages.label: has(email)?
messages.note: The fake answers from an in-memory `Set`. No database, so the test is fast and repeatable.

messages.label: false
messages.note: The email is new, so the service carries on.

messages.label: add(email)
messages.note: The fake stores it for real, so a second call will see it.

messages.label: send(email, 'Welcome')
messages.note: The spy sends nothing. It only records the call in its `sent` list.

messages.label: 'OK'
messages.note: Assert on the return value: an output check.

messages.label: read sent
messages.note: Assert on the recorded call: interaction testing. Both checks prove the behaviour, not the internals.

code.title: Fake and spy by hand
code.caption: TDD step: add a test that `register('')` returns `'INVALID'`. Run it red, then make it green.

walk.text: Both collaborators arrive through the constructor. That seam is what makes the class testable.
A fake: a working, in-memory stand-in for a user store.
A spy: records each call so the test can inspect it later.
A tiny runner. Real projects use `node --test`; the idea is the same.
Arrange, act, assert. Fresh doubles per test keep tests independent.
The edge case: a duplicate must not send a second email.

code.title: Built-in mock.fn
code.caption: Node's `node:test` module ships `mock.fn()`, a stub that also records its calls.

pitfalls: Double only collaborators at the class's edge; mocking internal helpers ties tests to internals.
Assert observable behaviour, not private fields or the order of internal calls.
Create fresh doubles in every test, or one test's calls leak into the next.

quiz.why: Only levels above 2 call `send`. Levels 3 and 5 qualify, so the spy records two calls.

takeaway: Inject collaborators, swap in doubles, and write the failing test first.
